interpretation.allocated_bytes: Not measured: adding an allocator instrumentation dependency was not justified and no suitable dependency was already locked.
interpretation.flat_baseline_scope: The flat baseline scans the same normalized active LTM center keys and returns distance-only top-k; it excludes projection, record support, and hydration.
interpretation.idempotency_limit: Unique idempotency events remain durable until the 64 MiB source-basis quota rejects further ingestion. VACUUM/checkpoint compaction does not prune them.
interpretation.kernel_only_warning: Kernel-only latencies are pre-embedded and are not full-text recall latencies.

controls.mutant_caught: Removing the max_record_bytes check makes the expected BudgetExceeded assertion fail; mutating before validation changes the digest equality assertion.
controls.name: record_16k_pre_mutation

controls.mutant_caught: A dynamic-growth or silent-reinforcement mutant makes the CapacityExhausted assertion fail; a non-atomic mutant changes the record count.
controls.name: fixed_center_capacity

controls.mutant_caught: Removing the encode-side frame check makes the expected Oversized assertion fail.
controls.name: wire_request_bound

controls.mutant_caught: Removing the preflight makes the second append succeed; checking after INSERT changes source_basis_bytes despite the rejected transaction assertion.
controls.name: source_basis_quota

controls.mutant_caught: Dropping events/checkpoint state during compaction or replay makes either post-compact or post-reopen digest equality fail.
controls.name: checkpoint_compact_reopen_retention

controls.mutant_caught: Removing top_k, advance, or LRU bounds respectively changes the rejection outcomes or resident_namespaces == 4 assertion.
controls.name: engine_topk_advance_resident_bounds

controls.mutant_caught: An unbounded mailbox yields zero Busy results; removing kill escalation makes the <=400 ms cancellation assertion fail.
controls.name: ipc_mailbox_and_cancellation

data.negative_control_rule: Each passing control names the assertion that a no-op or bound-removal mutant would fail.
